Interface Text.Pattern

All Known Implementing Classes:
Text.Affix
Enclosing class:
Text
public static sealed interface Text.Pattern permits Text.Affix (not exhaustive)
Selects at most one occurrence in a text, to extract, remove or replace it.

Conditions select the first or last occurrence that satisfies all of them, not the first or last occurrence if it does. They are checked against the whole text, right before or right after the occurrence, and are not part of it: first('@').followedBy("gmail.com") selects only the @. Each condition returns a new pattern and leaves this one unchanged.

A match of a regular expression that fails a condition is skipped, never shortened: the search resumes one character after its start. So first(Pattern.compile("\\d+")).followedBy("5") finds nothing in "1235".

A pattern is immutable and thread-safe.

Since:
0.1.3

    • replaceFrom

      String replaceFrom(CharSequence text, String replacement)
      Replaces the occurrence this pattern selects in text. The replacement is literal: unlike with Matcher.replaceFirst(String), $ and \ have no special meaning.
      Parameters:
      text - the text to search
      replacement - the text to put in place of the occurrence
      Returns:
      text with the occurrence replaced, or unchanged if there is none
